item.title: Video: Why are Republicans hosting a midterm convention?
item.description:
EXCLUSIVE — DALLAS — With an eye toward energizing the GOP's MAGA base, the Republican National Committee (RNC) on Tuesday announced the speaking order and times of this week's first-ever GOP midterm convention, and President Donald Trump will be the Primetime headliner both nights. According to the list , which was shared first with Fox News Digital on the eve of the convention, the president will deliver Wednesday's keynote address, which is tentatively scheduled to start at 9 p.m. ET. Trump will return on Thursday evening at the American Airlines Center in downtown Dallas to close out the convention, with remarks after Vice President JD Vance gives the second night's keynote speech. item.title: Western Hawaii islands survey damage after Hurricane Lowell passes by
item.description:
A satellite closeup of Hurricane Lowell on Sept. 8, 2026, after it passed just west of Kauai in the Hawaiian Islands. NASA The Hawaiian Islands rarely see significant hurricane damage , but they just experienced the effects of their second hurricane in a year as Hurricane Lowell’s eyewall brushed Niihau, west of Kauai, on Sept. 8, 2026. The hurricane brought heavy downpours, high surf and hurricane-force wind gusts that pounded both islands, knocking out power and flooding roads . Tropical storm conditions reached as far as Honolulu on the island of Oahu. A video from Kauai shows the damage during Hurricane Lowell. ABC News. Lowell was the 14th named Pacific storm of 2026 and the fifth hurricane. item.title: How has Israel hit back against sanctions by the UK, others?
item.description:
Israel hit back at the UK for leading a twelve-country alliance that is restricting trade with Israeli settlements in the West Bank, a grouping that showcases the growing closeness between Europe and Canada. Analysts said the measures against settlement building, illegal under international law, were more symbolic than tangible. But the curbs nevertheless marked the latest example of Western countries — notably excluding the US — banding together in sometimes informal groupings on issues ranging from support for Ukraine to trade. That cooperation looks set to grow with Canada’s prime minister due to address the European Parliament next week . Recent events have even pushed the “fringe” notion of Canadian membership in the EU “ into mainstream conversation ,” a New Yorker writer noted. — Prashant Rao

item.title: Why is France so good at animation?
item.description:
Until last week, a big electric-blue sculpture by Joel Shapiro sat next to the Kennedy Center. Boxy and rigid but seemingly weightless, Blue looked like a clumsy person who’d been swept by a breeze into an accidental pirouette. Shapiro called the metalwork a “celebration of possibility.” Some people thought it looked like Gumby. I loved it. The leaders of the Kennedy Center—and there is really just one leader of the Kennedy Center—did not. Workers dismantled Blue last Wednesday. No specific reason was given, save that the change had occurred at the center’s request. Internal documents obtained by The New York Times say that the sculpture was targeted for removal soon after Donald Trump took control of the institution. item.title: Russia and Ukraine exchange strikes as two killed at Moldova border
item.description:
An overnight Russian drone strike at a border crossing between Ukraine and Moldova killed at least two people, Odesa's regional governor said Wednesday. Moldovan Prime Minister Vasile Tofan said that 17 drones had hit Moldovan territory in August alone as both Kyiv and Moscow ramp up long-range strikes on military and energy infrastructure.

item.title: Which countries banned goods from settlements but trade with Israel?
item.description:
France and Canada joined the UK in announcing trade sanctions on Israel’s West Bank settlements Tuesday, as rising settler violence in the occupied territory widened a geopolitical rift between Israel and its allies. They are among 12 nations that signed a letter condemning Israel for “ undermining the possibility of a two-state solution.” UK foreign secretary Ed Miliband has vowed a “comprehensive reset” of relations with Israel, drawing sharp remonstrance from the White House, which threatened trade countermeasures against the UK. London’s newfound assertiveness reflects a “post-American turn,” former UK government adviser Ben Judah argued: In marshaling a European coalition against Israeli settlements, “the UK has found a role and an influential one, partially as a consequence of America abandoning hers .” — Brendan Ruberry

item.title: A journalist coined ‘the Bible Belt’ 100 years ago – it’s been oversimplifying the South ever since
item.description:
Even when the phrase was coined, the 'Bible Belt' image depicted just a portion of the region's culture. John Hayes “Look No Further!” a billboard on the side of the highway beckons, drawing my gaze toward the red cover of a Bible. “You Are Worthy of Redemption!” Not far away, another sign urges me to “Keep Christ in Christmas.” Then farther down the road a third appears: “Jesus: COMING SOON” its bright colors announce. Signs like these are familiar to me: I’m a historian who studies the U.S. South and lives in it. I know how easily they can evoke the South – or, I should say, a certain image of it. As that image pictures it, the South is “the Bible Belt”: a place where people are really religious, and, as a result, socially and politically conservative.
